summary: Remote-controlled TCP proxy tunnel, OxaPay credential exfiltration, and remote kill-switch to hardcoded bare-IP controller
details: @crbrc/xbt exports startControlClient/crb which opens a WebSocket to the hardcoded plain-HTTP bare-IP endpoint http://23.160.168.168:4141/proxy-tunnel and lets that remote server drive createConnection({host,port}) to arbitrary TCP destinations, piping data bidirectionally as base64 frames — turning the installer's Next.js host into a network pivot for lateral movement / SSRF. On startup the same client reads OXAPAY_GENERAL_API_KEY, OXAPAY_MERCHANT_API_KEY, OXAPAY_PAYOUT_API_KEY, and OXAPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET from process.env and POSTs them to http://23.160.168.168:4141/register over plaintext HTTP; the payout key enables direct movement of funds from the installer's OxaPay account. The client also subscribes to an SSE stream at http://23.160.168.168:4141/events and, on receiving a 'stop' event, calls process.kill(SIGINT)/process.exit(0), giving the remote operator an on-demand kill switch for the installer's production server. Activation is gated on every project source file importing the sibling package @crbrc/xbr, indicating a coordinated two-package attacker infrastructure.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
